title: Canada dominates Sweden 5-1 at women's hockey worlds opener
summary: Jessie Eldridge scored twice and added an assist as Canada defeated Sweden 5-1 Friday in its world women's hockey championship opener.

image.caption: Canada's Rebecca Leslie, right, celebrates after scoring a goal with teammate Daryl Watts (95) against Sweden on Friday in Herning, Denmark. (Bo Amstrup/Ritzau Scanpix via The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Hockey
Jessie Eldridge scored twice and added an assist as Canada defeated Sweden 5-1 Friday in its world women's hockey championship opener.
Jessie Eldridge scored twice as Canadians skate away with 5-1 victory
Eldridge started on Canada's top line and ably filled the void left by injured captain Marie-Philip Poulin and star forward Sarah Fillier.

items: New-look Canadian women's hockey team has an eye on the future
Canada, U.S. will wear generic jerseys at the women's worlds due to commercial rights dispute

blocks.text: The 28-year-old, from Barrie, Ont., who recently signed a two-year contract with the Professional Women's Hockey League champion Montréal Victoire, made her only other appearance at the women's world championship in 2022, where she had two points in seven games.
Defender Cooper Kendall had a goal and an assist for Canada, while Emily Clark and Rebecca Leslie also scored.
Jesse Eldridge leads Canada past Sweden at the worlds
Hanna Thuvik had Sweden's only goal.
Ann-Renée Desbiens made 11 saves for Canada. Ebba Svensson Traff stopped 33 shots for Sweden.
Canada next faces Japan on Sunday.
In Group A, the Czech Republic had to rally to beat Austria 4-1. Austria is playing in the top division for the first time. Katerina Mrazova led the Czechs with two goals and an assist.
Defending champion the United States opens later Friday against Switzerland in Group A and last year’s bronze medalist Finland faces host Denmark in Herning.
North America's rivalry
The U.S. and Canada are the tournament favorites, continuing a long-standing cross-border rivalry. Canada has won 13 world titles followed by the U.S. with 11 spanning the previous 24 championships.

The Americans have won 10 of the past 14 worlds and claimed the 2025 title in the Czech Republic and the Olympic gold medal at the Milan Cortina Games in February, beating Canada in overtime in both finals.
Finland is the only other team apart from Canada and the U.S. to reach the final, doing so in 2019.
The 11-day, 10-nation tournament in the Danish cities of Esbjerg and Herning is the first to take place in November after the IIHF moved it to open before the Professional Women's Hockey League.
Rather than having the top five teams grouped together as before, the field has been split into two groups of five based on rankings, with the U.S. leading one group and Canada the other.
The top four from each group qualify for the playoffs with the final set for Nov. 16.
The bottom two will play a relegation game.
Jersey dispute
Canada and the U.S. wear generic jerseys without their logos mandated by the International Ice Hockey Federation that were designed by IIHF supplier True Hockey.
Why Team Canada is wearing generic jerseys at women's hockey worlds
Hockey Canada and USA Hockey have their own apparel and jersey contracts with Bauer and CCM, respectively.
The two have been suing the IIHF over the dispute at a Swiss court.
With files from The Canadian Press
